Request scope and fee

From enquiry to a defined engagement

  1. Ask about availability. Send only your preferred package and contact details. Do not attach complaints, names of other parties or evidence.
  2. Complete a conflict check. The provider must confirm independence, professional eligibility and capacity before accepting work. Any identifying information needed for that check is requested through a separately agreed secure channel.
  3. Agree the offer. Receive the named provider, exact deliverables, fee and applicable taxes, turnaround, clarification window, cancellation/refund terms and secure handling arrangements in writing before payment.
  4. Prepare and review. Work remains your own factual account. Review every draft before using it; deadlines continue independently of this service.
  5. Close the engagement. Receive the agreed materials and a next-step checklist; any further work requires a new written scope.
Service limits and professional independence

No fabricated facts, coached testimony, credibility score, finding of guilt, outcome guarantee or influence over the Committee. This is not an emergency service or an automatic lawyer appointment. No representation before the Committee is included: applicable Central Rule 7(6) excludes legal practitioners from representing parties before the Committee. Any separate advice must comply with the applicable law and professional duties.

A provider must not accept conflicting engagements. Committee assistance and individual support in the same matter require an independence review; declining or referring an engagement must remain possible. Buying individual support does not give priority in the Committee process.

Read the Central Rules
Privacy and records

Navigator stores account and plan access only, never case information. This page has no case upload or intake form. A personalised engagement can begin only after separate secure handling, retention and deletion arrangements are agreed; ordinary enquiry email must not contain case material.
